subject: Adaptive Efficiency Offer — quant + batching guardrails & discount request
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@helixcommerce.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Explore Optimize Toolkit pricing for Helix pilot

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran a quick internal sizing exercise and think there's a clear opportunity to reduce per-request cost if we push more inference to a cache-first model and use a quantized 4-bit variant for conversational scoring.

Before we commit to a pilot, the finance team has asked for a clear pricing structure and an upfront discount for a 3-month pilot (~$45k expected usage). Specifically we need:
- A breakdown of how batching & prefix/KV caching would be credited against usage (do cached tokens count?)
- Recommended quantization profile (4-bit vs 8-bit) with expected latency and quality impacts on our QPS
- Any pilot-only discounts or credits you can offer to align risk

Attached is our anonymized call volume and example sessions (link to Drive). Happy to jump on a short call.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Platform, HelixCommerce

(attachment referenced: helix_volume_sample.csv)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Explore Optimize Toolkit pricing for Helix pilot

Elena —

Appreciate the context and the sample traffic. High level answers up front:
- Cached tokens: by default Redwood does not bill for tokens served entirely from the KV/prefix cache; billing applies to tokens computed by the model. We can surface cache hit rate estimates so finance can forecast savings.
- Quant profile: 4-bit (QLoRA-style) generally shows ~1.2-1.5x throughput improvement vs 8-bit with a small accuracy delta depending on model family; we can run a quick A/B on your representative prompts.
- Pilot discounts: we typically structure pilot credits + a sliding discount that scales with committed peak QPS/commit band. Marcus will propose a clean commercial sketch for a 3-month pilot and a ramp to commit.

Connor — can you take point on a short techncial note for Elena outlining expected latency at different cache hit rates and quant profiles? Marcus — can you draft a simple pilot econ sheet (credits + discount tiers) and a one-page mutual action plan?

I'll block 30 minutes for mid-week if that helps.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference | makers of the Optimize toolkit

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-21T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot economics sketch — HelixCommerce (3mo)

Elena / team —

Attached is a draft commercial sketch that maps usage bands to proposed discounts and credits for a 3-month pilot. Key points:
- Pilot credit: $15k in platform credits applied up front to cover initial inference while we validate quality.
- Discount tiers: 5% at $50k/month commit, 10% at $100k/month, 15% at $200k/month. Pilot acceptance can count toward the first-month commit.
- Quantization uplift: we allow a one-time 10% usage credit if Helix deploys our verified 4-bit profile across the pilot (this is intended to offset any initial quality tuning work).
- Caching accounting: cached token savings will be modeled observable in the console; for contract purposes we bill only for non-cached tokens. We can include a reporting SLA for cache-hit metrics.

I've attached the XLSX that breaks numbers into commit bands and shows an example TCO at 60% cache hit, 2x batching efficiency, and rollout to a 4-bit profile.

Next steps: if this looks directionally good, we'll convert to a short MSA addendum + MAP (mutual action plan) and Connor will provide the cache/latency appendix.

Attachment: helix-quant-proposal.xlsx (commercial sketch)

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Commercials — Redwood Inference

From: Elena Morales <elena@helixcommerce.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T14:50:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics sketch — HelixCommerce (3mo)

Marcus / Mina —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. A few clarifying questions from our side before we share with finance: 
1) For the one-time 10% usage credit tied to 4-bit adoption — does that apply to billable tokens or to the invoice amount? We want clarity on net spend modeling.
2) If cached tokens are not billed, are we required to expose the cache to Redwood (i.e., share prefix lists) or can we keep caching logic client-side and still have hit metrics?
3) On the reporting SLA: what latency windows define a successful cache-read (e.g., if a cache retrieval costs 5ms vs model generation 75ms, is that included in your SLO calculation)?

Finance is sensitive about "pilot credits" that just move spend across months; they prefer explicit invoice credits or percentage-off that shows on the invoice. Would you be open to converting the $15k credit into an invoice credit line item?

Happy to hop on the call you suggested — availability next Wed after 11am PT.

Best,
Elena

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@helixcommerce.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot economics sketch — HelixCommerce (3mo)

Elena —

Thanks for the great questions. Quick technical responses inline below and a short attachable appendix I hope you can share with finance: 

> 1) Does the 10% usage credit apply to billable tokens or invoice amount?

It applies to billed invoice amount (we can apply it as a line-item credit). That keeps your month-of-net-spend clean for internal reporting.

> 2) Are we required to expose cache listings to Redwood?

No — you can keep caching logic client-side. To provide reliable hit metrics we ask for a lightweight telemetry hook that sends anonymized cache-hit events (session id + hit/miss + token_count) — this can be throttled and signed. We do not need prefix contents.

> 3) Reporting SLA / latency windows for cache-read

Operationally we treat cache-read as a separate metric; our SLOs are for end-to-end 95th percentile tail. For your planning, assume cache-read adds 3-10ms depending on network topology; model generation at our default 8-bit path is ~55-120ms p95 depending on sequence length. 4-bit tends to shave ~20-35% off model generation p95. We'll include a short appendix with expected numbers across your sample sessions.

We are OK converting the $15k pilot credit into an invoice credit line item — Marcus will update the commercial sketch to reflect that. Also attaching a short latency extract from a similar pilot (anonymized) so you can see the delta when cache hits approach 60%-70%.

Attachment: kv-cache-latency-report.pdf (anonymized pilot extract)

If you'd like, we can lock the 10% invoice-credit-for-4bit adoption into the MAP and require a simple post-pilot QC check (A/B on 300 prompts) to verify no meaningful quality regression.

Connor O'Brien
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
